body: The beach is extremely crowded in January. You have to look a bit for a good spot to lie down between all the people, but once you’re settled it’s perfect. The bright sun, soft sand and refreshing sea make this beach ideal. The only downside is that there are also a lot of surfers in January, zig-zagging through the water. You have to watch out so you don’t get hit by a surfboard. It would be better if they separated a surfing area and a swimming area for everyone’s safety.
title: Crowded, but lovely

body: Hiriketiya Beach is a stunning horseshoe-shaped bay on Sri Lanka’s south coast, known for its turquoise water, soft sand, and year-round surf. The vibe is laid-back with cozy cafés, yoga spots, and boutique stays. It’s perfect for swimming, beginner surfing, relaxing, and enjoying a trendy yet peaceful beach atmosphere.
title: Hiriketiya Beach

body: My daughter had a lesson yesterday with Surf Monkey. The lesson itself was good but later we were asked to pay LKR 35 000 for a crack in the board. We were not asked to check the board before the lesson so don't know if the crack was already there. The boards are well used and not in good condition. Our board was used appropriately during the lesson and any crack would be normal wear and tear so not our responsibility. We initially refused to pay but then discovered that the instructor had hired the board from the neighboring business Utopia Surf School. Our instructor offered to pay himself but this seemed unfair so we, reluctantly, paid ourselves. After this incident I did some research and see that this is a frequent scam at Hiriketiya and Utopia Surf School have some history here. My disappointment and anger at this situation was exacerbated by the sniggering attitude of the Utopia Surf School people when I handed over the money.
title: Hiriketiya Surfboard Hire Scam

body: The views are simply stunning, with palm-fringed shores and clear blue water. Many tourists were enjoying surfing in the bay, and the early morning vibe was so peaceful and refreshing. A perfect hidden paradise on Sri Lanka’s south coast!

body: Heaven on earth! Kima Hiriketiya surf camp is an absolute dream. The surf guides & managers, the resort staff & social hosts, the owner Jimmy and friends all made my stay incredible, I had the best time. The food all day is all delicious esp breakfast plus Sri Lanka night and BBQ, the Mango “Megan” Margaritas 🤣 ( self named) to die for, scheduling surf lessons, surf skate, yoga, ice baths video analysis and theory all brilliant, property is an oasis with incredible sunset beach nearby, and I love Scooter the house pet and local wildlife everywhere and local temple tour was beautiful and trip to Yala National Park phenomenal but most of all the care and patience and absolute LOVE given to everyone makes my heart break a little to leave. body: Hiriketiya Beach is one of the places we had heard least about when we were planning our 3 week trip around Sri Lanka. I wouldn’t quite call it the hidden gem of the south coast, as it is growing in popularity, but it’s not too far off it.The neighboring town, Dikwella (known locally as Dickwella), has become a huge draw to people visiting Sri Lanka’s south coast. The laid-back lifestyle and surf vibes at Hiriketiya Beach and Dikwella have created those amazing coastal towns we absolutely love. The result is this magnetic draw similar to other trendy surf towns worldwide, whether it is Siargao in the Philippines, Tofino in Canada or Margaret River in Australia – people love the environment it creates. The fun atmosphere and dreamy setting make it an incredible place to spend a few days. There are loads of awesome things to do, cheap places to eat and endless waves to surf.
title: excellent place to visit

body: Absolutely loved this beach, the vibe, and the views. If you want to chill, swim, snorkeling or surf - this place is the right one. Away from crowds with a few places to eat, drink and get a sunbed. You can rent surfboards (very cheap) in here . There are 2 surfing areas: the main beach break (perfect for beginners) and a fast left wave in the Eastern side of the beach. I was surfing when green turtles popped up right under me! That was so unique. The vibe in the water is also incredible - people surfing here are very cheering and happy. No screaming or unnecessary competition for waves. It's just perfect. So far my favorite beach in Sri Lanka ! The western side of the beach is very calm and no waves if you want to swim and snorkel. Upon consuming something at the beach bar you can use the sunbeds without any extra charge (opposite to most places in Unawatuna, Dalawella or Mirissa).
title: Gorgeous place - one of the best beaches in Sri Lanka

body: Between 10am and 5pm you can walk from one end of this beach to the other across the loungers and then back again over the surf on top of the boards without getting any sand or sea in-between your toes. Despite this it’s a beautiful bay that we had more or less to ourselves at sunrise every morning. You can also find a nice spot under a tree to read your book away from the bars that play non-stop reggae. Businesses have grown organically along the beach and it’s just a matter of time before more established hotels take over. C’est La Vie! There are some great places to eat and sleep near Hiri beach. If you’re looking for a quiet, chilled-out, deserted spot then head to Dikwella beach and the guys at Machan’s hut will sort you out with a magical g&t.
title: Sunrise Swims

body: This beach is known to be a recently developed destination in Sri Lanka. The tourist area is concentrated around lovely beach of a small bay that is surrounded by a green thicket. The area is full of budget accommodation, restaurants facing the beach and a range of water sports. The water sports equipment are available to hire at reasonable costs. Local community is extremely hospitable towards the tourists. I must visit if you love serene beaches.

body: If you’re reading this then you are about 2 years too late to visit what used to be Sri Lankas most beautiful beach.What was once a postcard is now covered with foam board rental shops and bob marley playing tiki bars, with rubbish strewn everywhere, plastic bottles and straws lapping in the water, and beginner surfers dropping in on anybody catching a wave.Go at sunrise to catch a glimpse at what once was, get your instagram shot, and be gone elsewhere after 5 minutes before it’s descended on by the mob.
title: The beach formerly known as....

body: Best is to go early morning around 6:30am or at 5pm to avoid the harsh sun and the crowd. The sea is very calm and you can swim in it. There are no corals so does not make sense trying to snorkel. The sea has small waves so its ideal for those who want to learn how to surf since the sea is not rough. There are many shops by the beach renting out surf boards for Rs. 500/- per hour and giving instructor lessons for Rs. 3,000/- per lesson. They also rent out sun lounge chairs for Rs. 300/- per hour and there are many shops that sell drinks, food and alcohol. There are many restaurants nearby where you can have lunch and dinner from and the rates per person are between Rs. 500/- to Rs. 2,000/- depending on what you order and where you eat from. What I hated was that it was overcrowded with too many surfers during the day time and local vendors trying to force foreigners to buy things and not giving you privacy.
title: Go early morning to avoid the crowd

body: Five of us, three adults and two kids stayed in a hotel from 22nd to 25th December 2019, close to the Hiriketya Beach with its lovely turquoise waters.The beach is in an oval shaped cove or a bay, sheltered on either side with two hillocks that protect the bay from strong winds. The calm shallow waters invite you with its appealing and turquois blue. There is no current and the waves are gentle. There were many surfers too, some closer to the beach, others further away closer to bay entrance. Surfing boards are available at Rs 500 per hour or Rs 1500 for the whole day. Three of us had surfing lessons from one of the many available instructors and the cost was Rs 9000 for two hours. Though surfing is available throughout the year, non-monsoonal months October to April are calm and preferable.All along this 500-metre-long beach are many cafes, restaurants and surfing board hires. Beach chairs are dotted all along with many guests enjoying the sun and this marvellous little beach at a rustic village in a hidden corner of Sri Lanka.Expect the beach to be crowded and full of tourists, surfers and swimmers during the season November to March.
title: Turquois Blue Gentle Waters – Surfers’ Paradise

body: We had stopped en route from Yala to Matara for what we hoped would be a quick swim in a quiet cove...Instead, the area around the beach was disappointingly chaotic, clogged with traffic, and virtually inaccessible. The rapidly developing area adjacent is too cramped to accommodate all the surfers and Instagram tourists.The beach is small, over-crowded, and consequently uninviting. Even our overheated kids were discouraged and didn’t want to stay.A far cry from the “most beautiful beach in the world” we’d read about.
title: Not what we expected

body: It's so sad to return to a beach that you visited 2 years previously (and that you still dream about) only to find that it's a totally different place. I stayed in the area for 4 days over Christmas and I was shocked at the state of this beach, and at the amount of people. Luckily I discovered Dikwella beach just next door for swimming in calmer waters and with it's beautiful sunsets. I went back to Tangalle, and also loved the beaches there, especially near Coconut Island. It doesn't seem to have changed at all in that area.

body: Due to unplanned development, the beach is eroding quickly and losing its charm. Garbage is becoming an issue. A few good spots to eat and chill (Dots, grove, salt house) but the surfing is tired and done. With all the local surf schools in the area congregating in this tiny bay there is no longer room to roam. Best of all there’s an out of touch territorial local-expat scene taking shape. Lots of ‘too-cool-for-school’ hipster attitude in the water. This place was pure magic a couple years ago, sadly that day is no longer.

body: Nice waves when we visited (July 20th) for 3 days. Waves were choppy, so not ideal for surfing (although several surfers were in the water).Super clear and clean turquoise water. It was also possible to swim.Some restaurants were opened having prices 5 to 8 times the value of a normal restaurant in Sri Lanka. Still a nice place to cool down after several weeks on the road.

body: We had just arrived to the Beach and rented a surfboard for the hour to make the most of the late afternoon.Having a great and pleasant time until my husband hands back the board and then a young lad tries calling us over and demand 20,000rupees because of a crack in the board (all boards heavily used and not in new condition clearly as such a busy beach) Obviously argued that we would not pay such an obscene figure and that all the boards in used condition and we honestly did not cause any damage. Owner then follows my husband to our beach table and harassed us some more. Trying to diffuse the situation my husband again tried to say we are not paying and the owner grabbed his shirt and tried to drag him behind the shop but he managed to shout and push himself away. Owner then comes down to itimidate me alone on the beach in front of everyone.This surf stall is towards the west end of the beach with a simple black and white sign.Absolutely appalled by this behaviour - we are on our honeymoon and has left a bad impression of Sri Lanka. We returned to this country as we had visited before and know it had become very popular with tourists but we have never experienced such crookedness from the Sri Lankan people.Tourists are unfortunately being taken advantage of in these popular places and totally shocked at the intimidation and aggression.This beach is very busy - there is a lot of coastline to see so I do not recommend it as anything particularly special other then handy if you want to learn to surf but it is crowded.You will be targeted especially if you look vulnerable or like you have never surfed before (that’s clearly what happened to us).We are honest people and never normally leave a review but do feel people have to be wary of this place and this behaviour which we would have expected elsewhere but not in Sri Lanka. What a shame the locals are acting like this.
title: Please read - Thugs on the beach

body: We rented 2 surfboards from the surfshop. They didn't make you sign anything which I thought was pretty carefree. The boards were in ok shape, a bit damaged. However, when we went to return them they said we had cause a small scratch on one of the boards (which we had not). They wanted 70$ from us to "fix" it. When I said there was no way we were paying that and to call the police, they refused and wouldn't let us leave. They called several other guys and said if we didn't pay them then we really would have to call the police, essentially threatening us with violence. We ended up giving them 30$ and they snickered as we left. DO NOT RENT A SURF HERE. Or if you do, make sure to take pictures of the board.The beach itself is alright. Nothing special, ok waves for beginners although on the day we were there they were not very frequent. Also, it is way too crowded since it is on the smaller side.
title: DO NOT rent from the surfshop. They are thugs.

body: This beautiful patch of beach is wonderful, and really great for surfers. It has crystal blue waters, tiny fish, good waves and plenty of places with surf boards to rent. There are lots of beach bars and cafes too. The drawback? It's nowhere near as idyllic as other beaches around Sri Lanka as it's just full of white tourists, and so the businesses are tailored to thAt, the food is very western and so are the prices. There are some other amazing beaches nearby with very few people on, if any, and that is much more preferable to us!
title: Great beach, only for tourists

body: Hiriketiya is a hidden beach reachable by taking a right turn @ Dodampahala junction beyond Dickwella town on Tangalle/Hambantota Mahawela) road. Within a few hundred meters you have to turn right right again on to a bad quality road (April 2019) leading up to the beach. Just follow Google Maps if you don't want to find the way on your own. I cannot find the right words to describe the graciousness of the place. It's an exceptional gradient of colors in the waters that attracted me first. It's simply magical. Breaking of waxes creates miriads of different patterns in the water that pleases the eye even more. Surfers from different parts of the world gather here practice their hobby. This beach is, in fact, a small bay guarded by a rocky mouth. And the beach is well shaded making it really cool even during hot days. There are a number of guest houses offering good quality accomodation and meals. For visitors who are not staying vehicle parking is an issue at the moment. However, situation can be expected to improve in the near future. Local authorities should pay more attention to this beach that is gaining recent popularity. The land value here is sky rocketing. There is a yellow minibus permanently parked by the beach, and is converted to a restaurant. Make sure that you visit this pristine beach when you travel this part of the island, even if you are not a surfer. But, please do not pollute the the surroundings of this amazing world.
title: Beach with outstanding beauty

body: I would absolutely not recommend visiting here with a girlfriend/ as a girl. Due to the influx of tourism in the main hotspots of Sri Lanka, the logical move is to travel further along the coast to get away from the crowds. Hiriketiya is a little less busy than the traditional hotspots (Hikkaduwa/ Weligama/ Galle/ Matara). But visiting a coastal village that has not yet fully caught up to the tourist boom has some stark drawbacks which any girl should be aware of before visiting. Hiriketiya has a very high population local males, and unfortunately the pervasive sense of sexual threat when walking around ranges from moderate to severe. Expect large groups of men hanging around, staring extremely menacingly and leaning in as you walk past. Driving past in scooters, stopping to make lewd comments and then driving away, It’s a really really nasty predatory vibe if female and both myself and my girlfriend felt at times, extremely unsafe. They also have a problem with street dogs biting people, we heard several reports of people being bitten at night during our stay. We were advised by several people to be careful. At night in our hotel room you can just hear a cacophony of barking all around, so I would be careful being out in Hiriketiya at night if you haven’t had a rabies vaccination, or if you happen to be female.
title: Word of warning- be very careful if female

body: This beach is excellent to swim, relax and surf. Quite a large bay but not much beach to relax. Learning to surf is available together with hiring surf boards
title: The Beach to be

body: We stayed here for a few days before moving on to Polhena. The beach is really beautiful and a great spot for watching surfing but it was hard to find space to sunbathe as the tide comes in quite far at times. The beach was also very busy. There are plenty of guest houses and restaurants nearby. The restaurants we found were quite fancy and pricier than we had been paying in other parts of Sri Lanka, it was easy to get hold of western food if wanted so it felt a bit like you could be anywhere.
title: Pretty but busy beach

body: A really picturesque beach in the south of Sri Lanka, probably one of the prettier beaches, but it is starting to get crowded. There are a ton of places to stay just off the beach both guest houses, and small villas for rent.
title: Beautiful Beach

body: One of the most beautiful beach and surfing spot in Sri Lanka. This hidden Hiriketiya beach became famous few year ago. Now a lot of tourist and surfing lovers visit Hiriketiya.
title: Amazing Surfing Spot in Sri Lanka

body: This Beach is one of the most beautiful in Sri Lanka, but sadly it has been abused by a serious lack care. This beach is also very over crowded and it makes me very sad, much better to go and chill at the beautiful open and empty Dikwella Beach.
title: A Beautiful Rubbish Dump

body: Hiri beach is the most pristine and beautiful beach in Sri Lanka. It is very crowded in season but this is because it is the perfect paradise destination. Get there early to secure a sun lounger, kick back and learn to surf, enjoy watching others and take a dip in the gentle waves. There are plenty of accommodation options and places to eat, drink and be merry. Dedicate at least 2 nights to this spot!
title: Best Bay in Sri Lanka

body: Good beach to have bath but over crowded and bit polluted still better than Polhena beach in Matara town.
title: Good beach to have bath

body: The beach is way too crowded and it's difficult to find a spot for your towels - or a sun bed after 11 am. Also the scene is nothing special.. and not good for swimming. Loved the nearby end of Dickwella beach - very quiet, plenty of space, sunbeds, coconuts, beer.. and the same scene.. not for surf though but good for swimming.
title: Only if surfing

body: This beach is a nice sheltered bay, where you can swim and surf withour being hit by the huge waves and the strong current which is common at the southern part of Sri Lanka. There are a few restaurants on the beach, they provide beach chairs if you eat or drink there.
title: Nice sheltered bay

body: We left our bag with the surf school just in front and to the left of the roti place as soon as you arrive to the beach. The same place we rented boards from.We came out the water and found one of the surf instructors going through our bag and stealing money. He was caught red handed. This obviously wasn’t the first time he had done it, by the reaction of the other guys working there. He didn’t take all the money just a couple thousand rupees, enough that we might not have noticed if we didn’t catch him actually with his hands in our bag taking it.
title: keep an eye on your belongings here.

body: This beach is certainly beautiful, no doubt about that. The drawbacks are that it's narrow and steeply sloped, so there's only so much room to put your towel. Very little shade available without renting a sun bed. One end is good for swimming and suitable for small children (with caution). Several food sellers, with the usual sea-side markup on food and drinks. Being a non surfer I was still able to enjoy myself, as the views are very nice, but felt like grandpa the old man amidst all of the "kids".
title: Beauty, but crowded

body: A stunning little cove like bay lined with palm trees - what more could you want? Well, less people. Due to the nature of the beach you do feel as though if you roll over on your towel, you may end up squashing the person next to you... If peace and quiet are your thing, avoid. However, if crystal clear water and the utmost feeling of a tropical beach are, then this is the place to be for an afternoon.
title: Stunning

body: The beach is ok not better than many others in Sri Lanka, way too far from being the best one in the south coast. It is packed with chairs up to the water line and surfers + hipsters. The narrow stretch of coarse sand (and stones) can't handle the ammount of people. The only reason to come here is for the good waves to surf or watching good surfers on the left (East) side. Anyway this place need traffic lights in the ocean too :(. A few overpriced options to eat nearby. There are much better places to go in Sri lanka if you need to enjoy a nice beach with an authentic local mood. Maybe it is just a matter of taste, It is simply not for me, and for many others as I can see.
title: Overcrowded and hispetered, hence overpriced. You've been warned.

body: Our driver stopped to show us this beach on our way from Mirissa to Tissa. I wish I had known it existed! It is a little slice of heaven, a small bay with perfect surf. A couple of foreigner run cafes in the area reminded me of Byron Bay, Tulum, Seminyak... very cool vibes.
title: I wish I had known!

body: This is the only beach so far where there has not been any available seats at any of the beach side restaurants. The beach is really small and cozy. Good for surfing beginners and apparently also for families with kids. Supposedly this beach was a lovely hidden gem just a few years ago but the tourists have unfortunately come to stay.
title: Fantastic small beach subjected to overcrowding

body: Pretty cove.A few bars. 1 restaurant. We think we did perfect combo came at 4pm had drinks and chilled then quick early dinner.Not loads here.Sure if you are a surfer very cool we enjoyed watching those braver than us. Few toddlers seemed content.Lots of young nimble bodies! Felt very old at 36 🤣Worth a short trip for sure 🌴
title: Cool crescent to watch surfers

body: We came to this beach thinking we would stay for 3 nights but had to leave the next morning, this beach is just a tourist trap, everything is made for tourists so the prices are higher than anywhere else we have been in Sri Lanka. There is no Sri Lankan culture , just a nice beach made to look like paradise for the vacationers. Its is away from the towns so they have all made the prices about the same and high and you dont really have a choice but to just keep spending your money.I honestly just felt like a dollar sign walking around and couldn't get out quicker. I didn't feel like anything was genuine. And then of course to get out of there you have to take a tuktuk that is 5 times the normal price.Quite disappointed.
title: Not for budget travellers at all

body: This beach is magic, clear waters, calm near the shore with a little surf break further out. Just gorgeous. We stayed about 15km away on Goyambokka beach, where accomodation was more suited to our family as Hiriketiya is oriented towards backpackers. But Hiriketiya beach is a must visit, we spent the day there, boys hired a board from a beach vendor (very cheap) and surfed for a few hours, we had lunch and drinks on the beach. It wasnt too busy when we were there in October.
title: Paradise

body: we were lucky to discover this lovely beach and the bay which had high waves and was happy to see the surfers enjoying the waves. another corner was with some group enjoying sea bathing and could see the fishers boats on the beach and can imagine the friendly atmosphere with the hospitable Sri Lankans creating an inviting atmosphere for the foreign and local visitors.
title: A place for Surfers and a lovely beach for beach lovers.

body: Quieter than some of the other areas, lovely beach, sheltered bay. Still enough waves to have some fun. Many children playing in the surf. Small beach restaurants along the beach. Glad we came. We were there during off season, but the beach was calmer enough to swim. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Lovely sheltered beach

body: If there is a worldwide competition to find the prettiest beach in the world this one would have to come in the top 10.
title: Prettiest beach in the world

body: We found this on our way to Tangalle, passing Dikwella. The access road to the beach is not the best but the trouble is all worth because it's one of the beautiful beaches with turquoise blue sea in SL and a great surf spot. Also the best thing about it is it's less crowded (you will find mostly foreigners) and clean. So i would call it a gem. Ideal spot for a good swim, sun bathing and to Surf. There are plenty of people who will hire surf boards and some will teach you too. Waves are ideal for both swim and surf. Make sure you take towels with you if you plan to visit because it's so tempting for a swim here. This is by far one of my favourite beaches and bathing spots in SL.
title: Secluded, beautiful beach not to be missed

body: Had a great time with another family staying in a villa near the beach. We were sightly worried about going in August but had very nice weather the entire week, with the occasional rain and windy conditions.
title: Beautiful surfing yet protected beach

body: We were blown away by Hiriketiya Beach - it’s so gorgeous! It is what I would describe as paradise! Lovely sand and clean, crystal waters. There is very good surf too for surfers! There are tasteful and well-run bars and restaurants/guest houses on the beach front too! Lots of memories of delicious food and beer right on the beach! I will be recommending this beach to everyone - the best we have been to in Sri Lanka!!
title: Absolutely stunning!

body: I really liked this beach a lot! Nice cove that was great for surfing. There was a right and left point break in either side of the cove. Also, good waves for beginners in from the points. Plenty of board rentals. Good for swimming too. This place will be big soon
title: One of the best beaches in Sri Lanka

body: We spent 3 days here in February and loved it so much we came back for another 2 days. This was our favourite beach we visited by far! We spent time in Bentota, Unawatuna, Delawella, Wijaya, Mirissa and Tangalle, but Hiriketiya was our favourite!! The beach was calm, the weather beautiful and although busy, we never struggled to get ourselves a lounge by the water. There are a number of food options including great local food on the beach or Western-style dishes back on Hiriketiya Road. It is walking distance or a short, cheap tuk-tuk ride from Dickwella town which is easily accessible by local bus. There are a number of reasonably priced guesthouse options in Hiriketiya right by the beach, or more expensive yoga retreat-style accommodation options for those with higher budgets. Hiriketiya is an extremely family-friendly location with a calm, sheltered beach; but even as a young childless couple we loved our time here!! Would highly recommend! Pure Paradise!
title: Favourite beach in Sri Lanka!

body: Clean water, safe beach, great restaurants. I find it hilarious that other people rate it poorly because it’s over crowded. It is one of the best beaches one can visit- of course it’s over crowded! Beach was busy (so was the sea) but it had a great vibe and everyone was very happy to be in paradise. Loads of good surf for beginners. Don’t miss it.
title: Brilliant for families

body: We stopped here for a few hours and secured a couple of seats in one of the restaurants/bars along the beach. The water was clean and clear with some small waves ideal for those wanting to learn to surf.
title: Relaxing few hours on the beach

body: An amazing horseshoe bay, with a great vibe and manageable waves for beginners. A couple of bars provide cheap drinks and food along the beach. Surfboard hire is available with good condition boards available for very cheap (250rupee 1 hour, 1000 rupee all day). Highly recommended.
title: Great surf bay

body: Lovely beach ... Swimming in this beach is awesome and the waves are great for surfing and swimming.A bit narrow and crowded but overall a must to visit if you are passing by.
title: Wonderful!

body: This is a lovely beach. Fantastic for learning to surf with plenty of boards for hire along the beach for about €2 per hour. Great spots all along the beach for lunch and milkshakes.
title: Great for learning to surf

body: Very nice horseshoe bay, best at sunrise for me. Reefs for snorkelling on both sides.Surf: Seemed to be 2 or 3 peaks for surfers including a nice left for experienced surfers. Potential for a right off of the other side but didnt work while I was there. Very mellow wave, great for practice but not high performance (In Feb). There was also a nice vibe in the water, good job because it was very busy! Longboarders wave
title: Nice beach but busy

body: We really enjoyed our stay in Hiriketiya. On the first day we learned to surf then we extended our stay for a total of 5 nights. We met some great locals and tourists our age (20's - 30's) in the restaurants and out on the water waiting for waves. It's a great vibe there and we will be returning soon.
title: Great spot for learning surfing and meeting great people

body: The beach was recommended a lot but I must have changed a lot. It is very crowded and the beach is very narrow so it’s not that easy to find a single spot to lay on the beach. Furthermore surfing also seems very quite difficult because of the crowd.
title: Little bit disappointing

body: The beach is as beautiful as most beaches around. However, it is famous for surfing and a lot of tourists, thus it can get pretty crowded, especially because there is not much space on the sand because of the waves. I'd recommend to visit the natural pool at Medilla inestead, located on the stunning Tangalle Beach. The beach is endless and super empty. Only a few little huts are there to provide you with food and beverages.
title: Stunning but crowded beach

body: Stopped here on a moped journey back from Matara. The turnoff is not marked, but the minor road is on Google Maps, so found it after a u turn. Uneven track takes you to the beach. Narrow strip of sand in a fabulous horseshoe bay. Lots of longboard surfers in the middle, but great swimming right hand side. A little wave and some undertow. Crystal clear water. We'll worth the stop.
title: Stunning setting

body: We travelled here from Tangalle for the day and had high hopes after hearing good things from other travellers and from reading a review in a national newspaper at home. The beach is over crowded and FULL of stray dogs (more than other places). It is quite narrow so not much space to lie your towel.It seemed popular for the surfing crowd. I wouldn’t recommend going out of your way to see this place if you’ve not got much time. Nearby beaches such as Tangalle (for gorgeous quite long beaches) and Mirissa (lovely beach but a lot more tourists) are much better.
title: Much nicer beaches elsewhere

body: Lovely bay for swimming, surfing (beginners) and relaxing. Not crowded, some guesthouse, good prices. Recommendable for a few days
title: Beautiful tranquil bay

body: Was told to go and see this beach. Yes it’s beautiful, yes it’s great for learning to surf but it’s not great for young kids. The drop off is quite steep for kids swimming and then there are all the beginner surfers trying to learn and avoid bashing the children with their boards. I wouldn’t take kids here but as an adult yeah sure. It’s not my taste as I prefer quieter places. Didn’t stay long and retreated back to our secret beach.
title: Beautiful but not for us

body: Wonderful beach , ( great woodfire pizza on the beach ) 3 place to rent surfboards and 3 placks to est , wonderful small bay. A few nice Hotels and good restaurants , Jasper House we stayed at, great place
title: Mr Lennart

body: This hidden gem is well worth the trip wherever in Sri Lanka you're staying. It's a paradise lagoon with both a nice slow longboard wave consistently pumping as well as a faster left on a reef so there is surfing for everyone regardless of level. Three beach restaurants serves you both breakfast, lunch and dinner and one of them also offers massage. We arrived 06.30 am and wasn't able to leave until 6 pm thanks to this truly paradise place.
title: A truly paradise Beach

body: Wow! You need to go here! It's the most beautiful beach I've been to along the South coast! A perfect horse shoe bay with blue water and decent surf. There is a pretty shallow reef break to the left, but the wave is mellow so don't worry about it. And there is a good beginner surf spot right in front of the beach, beautiful clean waves with turtles frequently popping up next to you 😍The beach is super tranquil and just lovely! Not much budget food on the beach front, but we took a walk to the little town where it was more "backpack-priced"
title: A perfect postcard

body: Beautiful little beach with a groovy vibe. A couple of nice places to eat, coffee or a fresh drink. We had wood fired pizza which was very good.The water was very clean and it was a post card setting. Nice clean sand, coconut palms and some surfers further out. Waves were a but rough but it was great fun even with small children. (7 and 10 good swimmers).Not recommended if you want a calm place to swim. This beach is really as beautiful as it gets.
title: Stunning beach with great waves

body: We only came here as out TukTuk driver convinced us to try it instead of Goyambokka. We were so glad he did! The beach itself is beautiful and there are a few bars and restaurants but not so many that the whole of the beach is overrun. The water was calm enough to swim in but was still popular with surfers. Give it a try!
title: Gorgeous!

body: Commonly referred to as "secret beach", Hiriketiya (or Hiri as I like to call it) is becoming less and less secret; however, the charm of a picturesque bay nestled in the jungle is a secret worth sharing. My friends and I would travel to Hiri once or twice a month to snorkel with turtles, eat at Salt House (highly recommended breakfast burritos!), and surf for a few hours at either the beach break or the more challenging point break. It's actually the perfect spot to spend an entire day. Kids can be occupied, couples can enjoy quiet space, and groups of friends can run wild. If you're travelling around the Island, make Hiriketiya a must-see on the itinerary.
title: An oasis on the rise

body: We were at Hiriketiya Beach to surf and at first had a great time. We rented some surfboards at the place on the left side of the beach (if you look out into the ocean). After 10 minutes a rubber safety cord of a board ripped unsurprisingly, because they are simply, really old. When we brought it back they demanded us to pay 20$ for the cord of a 50$ surfboard. When I objected the owner tried to fight me and one of his buddies tried to explain to me, that we are all human and maybe I should just give the guy money, since he doesn't have much. Don't get boards from that place, since they're going to try to pick your pockets.
title: Tourist Rip Off

body: Wonderfull place and wonderfull beach for swimming.... The cafe/restaurants was a little expensive but nice anyway and really good lunch on the place that looks much like a coffee bar with lounge music.. a little in the back fro the beach... :)
title: We loved this place!!!
Very nice
body: Nice beach, perfect for surfers (beginners to good surfers). 3 nice restaurants on site where you can eat from srilankan food to pizzas and burgers. We loved it. It can be busy though

title: Beautiful scenic sheltered beach with surf
body: My boyfriend loves surfing and took me to this beach. It is one of the most beautiful beaches we have been to in Sri Lanka. Small beach with some lovely cafes with hammocks and shade, very relaxing and scenic. Many places to hire a good range of surfboards at a good price (250-500 rupees per hour depending on the board). Surfing suitable for experienced surfers at the point with some good waves, and also suitable for beginners with easy smaller waves in the bay. We loved this beach and came back the second day. There are a few options to stay here at guest house/hotel which we would do if we came back. We stayed at Tangalle which was about 20min drive away.

title: Beautiful not-so-secret beach
body: I was told that Hiriketiya beach was a stunning beach little known other than to a handful of surfers by a friend who had visited 3 years ago. It was indeed a stunning bay, however I would not quite agree with the secret part, as there were quite a few tourists lounging around on the beach. The adventure of finding the perfect deserted beach can wait when you have beauty like this!

title: Best curry in Sri Lanka
body: A nice and relaxed bay, with the best curry we've had in 3 weeks holiday in Sri Lanka (on which we ate curry every day).We spent a small week in Hiriketiya with our 2 year old son. Hiriketiya is a bay that is predominantly focused on tourism. The small town Dikwella is separated from it (nice local market on Saturdays!). So you're dependent of the restaurants on the beach (4 in total). The beach house (owned by a western guy) is busiest for lunch (has an explicit lunch menu and a western orientation). But for diner one must go to SEA BREEZE. By far the best restaurant for diner on this small strip (we tried all). Chef Tensin is an absolute talent who works with whatever fresh stuff he could get his hands on that day. We ate there 3 times and every time the curries were totally different and absolutely delicious. Concerning the bay. Yes the waves are a bit less big in this bay than in most other places, however, they're still pretty big and there still is a big undertow. As a result one still needs to be an experienced swimmer and you can't just let your toddler play in the surf...

title: Best beach! Like paradise! Wie im siebten Himmel! Красота!
body: If you want to see how paradise can look like, go to this beach. Очень красиво и приятно! Sehr sehr schön und noch nicht überfüllt. Sehr zu empfehlen! Very nice for surfing too!

title: A hidden gem but for how long
body: Beautiful beach! Can almost guarantee in next few years tourism will take over so go now while it's still a somewhat secret paradise.Only thing I couldn't help but notice was the amount of NAKED children on the beach. Some of them 8 or 9 years old - in my option, very inappropriate. Protect your kids from the high UV and also cover them up!!

title: Awesome beach. Nice and quite.
body: Wonderful quite beach which would be great for kids or if you are on a honeymoon. If you are looking to party maybe don't bother. I was here with two other mates and we just enjoyed the beach, had some fun small waves, and snokerlled and fished. Three places to eat. Dots beach house is good but really expensive. Hiriketiya beach house is nice. The other joint is shocking. Foods ok but takes at least an hour and a half to come out. We went three times. Twice for dinner and once for breaky. Go to either of the first two. It's a good place. Will prob get ruined by tourism over the next few years so go now!!
